notes:
Summary: Larkspur builds orchestration software for autonomous warehouse fleets. Primary requirement: deterministic inference for short control prompts (<=32 tokens) used in closed-loop decisioning and higher-latency telemetry embeddings (256-1024 tokens) for analytics. Interested in Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and network isolation; private deployment (VPC/on-prem) discussed for regulatory and latency reasons.

POC scope: performance benchmarking on Dedicated. Team wants:
- Throughput guarantees for concurrent control channels (target 5k concurrent lightweight reqs during peak across region).
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 120ms for control prompts, p99 <= 250ms; tail latency critical.
- Reserved GPU planning: evaluate 4xH100 vs 8xA100 equivalent footprints for cost/throughput tradeoff.
- SLA asks: 99.95% uptime, P1 response <1 hour, scheduled maintenance windows aligned to local night shift.

Representative workloads used in POC: short control utterances (average 20 tokens), telemetry summaries (512 tokens) for embeddings and vector search, bursty batch reranking for mission planning (2-3k tokens).

Testing plan notes:
- Load tests: synthetic clients simulating robot fleet (80/20 read/write pattern), ramp to 120% of forecasted peak RPS.
- Soak test: 48-hour at 80% sustained traffic to detect memory growth and GC pauses.
- Tail analysis: CI will capture p99.9 and device-level metrics (GPU memory, NVLink saturation).
- Model variants: baseline fp16 13B LLM, optimized int8/4-bit quantized variant for cost comparison.
- Fallbacks: policy to route to smaller 7B model when queue depth > threshold; test functional parity and latency difference.

Engagement comments: SE Ravi ran two design sessions. AE Maya negotiated sample SLA and a dedicated staging cluster for the test. Customer wants Redwood to provide an SLO/numeric proposal for inclusion in their procurement packet.

Customer quotes: "We need rock-solid tail latency — a single spike can cascade across the fleet."

Docs attached: POC plan + perf checklist + initial security answers.
